newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Small U.N. team to help with Algeria election.
newsitem.headline: Small U.N. team to help with Algeria election.

text.p: A small U.N. technical team will support the work of international observers invited to monitor June 5 parliamentary elections in strife-torn Algeria but the U.N. officials will not themselves serve as observers, a U.N. spokesman said on Monday.
He said this decision was based on the conclusions of a U.N. evaluation mission which recently visited Algeria after President Liamine Zeroual last month requested U.N. assistance with the poll.

The U.N. role will apparently be similar to that during presidential elections in November 1995, when a small U.N. team did not venture outside the capital and did not rule on the fairness of the voting.
Algeria has been without an elected parliament since 1992 when the authorities annulled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
The country has since been plunged into violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces in which about 60,000 people have been killed.

"The United Nations is ready to supply to the government of Algeria a small technical team to coordinate and support the work of the international observers who were invited on the occasion of the parliamentary elections," U.N. spokesman Juan Carlos Brandt said.
The U.N. role would be to "facilitate the international monitoring of the electoral campaign as well as the progress of the tallying of votes."

But the United Nations itself would "not observe the elections in order to ensure their proper course and its results, and similarly the organisation will not make any declaration regarding the elections," he added.
